extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners preparing US patent applications with nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence disclosures (and USPTO examiners)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality requirements for preparing the Sequence Listing XML and representing nucleotide/amino acid sequences in U.S. patent applications filed (or international filings) on or after July 1, 2022, according to 37 CFR and WIPO Standard ST.26 as incorporated in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "Modified nucleotide"
rubrics_metrics.description: A “modified nucleotide” includes any nucleotide as described in paragraph 3(f) of WIPO Standard ST.26 (as explained in MPEP § 2412.03(d)) other than the standard monophosphates (deoxyadenosine 3’-monophosphate, deoxyguanosine 3’-monophosphate, deoxycytidine 3’-monophosphate, deoxythymidine 3’-monophosphate, adenosine 3’-monophosphate, guanosine 3’-monophosphate, cytidine 3’-monophosphate, or uridine 3’-monophosphate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This MPEP section cross-references WIPO ST.26 paragraph 3(f) and MPEP § 2412.03(d). Use the ST.26 list/criteria to determine whether a nucleotide is "modified"; ordinary ribo/deoxyribo monophosphates listed above are excluded from the "modified" label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sequence identifiers in description, claims, and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: When the description or claims discuss a sequence that is set forth in the Sequence Listing XML, the sequence must be referenced by its sequence identifier preceded by “SEQ ID NO:” (or the like) in the text of the description or claims; when a sequence is presented in a drawing, reference must be made by sequence identifier either in the drawing or in the Brief Description of the Drawings where the correlation is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence identifiers used in text/drawings must correspond to the identifiers assigned in the Sequence Listing XML (§ 1.832(a)). This is required even if the sequence is also embedded in the specification or claims. Use of SEQ ID NO: is a shorthand and does not change 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements. When multiple sequences appear in a drawing, ensure the correlation between drawing items and their SEQ ID NOs is clear (e.g., list in Brief Description).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible shorthand referencing of fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence identifiers may be used to discuss and/or claim parts or fragments of a properly presented sequence (e.g., "residues 14 to 243 of SEQ ID NO:23"), and such fragments need not be separately presented in the Sequence Listing XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may rely on sequence identifier + residue ranges to claim or describe fragments; ensure the referenced parent sequence is present in the Sequence Listing XML and that numbering is consistent with the sequence enumeration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence identifiers do not alter 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sequence identifiers throughout the specification and claims provides a shorthand but does not alter the statutory disclosure or claim requirements under 35 U.S.C. 112(a) or 112(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume sequence identifiers relieve any written description, enablement, or claim definiteness obligations—these remain governed by 35 U.S.C. 112; identifiers merely simplify reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequential numbering of sequence identifiers in Sequence Listing XML
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disclosed nucleotide or amino acid sequence that meets § 1.831(b) must appear separately in the Sequence Listing XML and must be assigned a separate sequence identifier beginning with 1 and increasing sequentially by integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although each sequence must have a different number, sequences should, where practical, be presented in numerical order and in the order discussed in the application to ease reference. Include identical shorter regions (identical to part of a longer sequence) as separate sequences with their own identifiers when they meet the enumeration requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total number of sequences must match sequence identifiers (including skipped sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: The total number of sequences indicated in the Sequence Listing XML must equal the total number of sequence identifiers, whether followed by an actual sequence or represented as an intentionally skipped sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sequences are intentionally skipped, represent them as specified (see intentionally skipped sequences criterion). Do not leave gaps between sequence identifier numbers without using the prescribed representation for skipped entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of intentionally skipped sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An intentionally skipped sequence identifier must be represented by setting the SequenceData element with the sequenceIDNumber equal to the skipped identifier and the element INSDSeq_sequence to the string "000", with no values for INSDSeq_length, INSDSeq_moltype, INSDSeq_division, and without an INSDSeq_feature-table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 58 and 59 format exactly for skipped sequences so the Sequence Listing XML's total sequence count and identifier mapping remain consistent and machine-parseable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide sequence representation: single strand 5'→3' and double-strand rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide sequence must be represented only by a single strand in the 5’ to 3’ direction from left to right (or a direction that mimics 5’ to 3’). A double-stranded nucleotide sequence disclosed by enumeration of residues may be represented as a single sequence or as two separate sequences (each with its own identifier) where the two strands are fully complementary; or as two separate sequences where they are not fully complementary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include the 5’ or 3’ designations or similar in the sequence text. If representing both strands, choose either single or two-sequence representation consistent with ST.26 guidance and assign identifiers accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide numbering rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The first nucleotide presented in the sequence is residue position number 1. For circular sequences, the applicant must choose which nucleotide is residue position 1. Numbering is continuous through the sequence in the 5’ to 3’ direction (or mimicking direction); the last residue number must equal the number of nucleotides in the sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure numbering in any claims/feature tables matches the enumeration used in the Sequence Listing XML; choose and document residue 1 consistently for circular sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide symbol set and case
rubrics_metrics.description: All nucleotides in a sequence must be represented using the symbols listed in WIPO ST.26 Table 1 and only lower-case letters must be used. Any symbol used represents exactly one residue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only the allowed lower-case symbols; do not use upper-case for nucleotides. Verify that each symbol corresponds to a single residue as required for machine readability and conformity with ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of symbol 't' and modified-base reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The symbol 't' will be construed as thymine in DNA and as uracil in RNA. Uracil in DNA or thymine in RNA are considered modified nucleotides and must be represented in the sequence as 't' and further described in a feature table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 't' represents an unusual context (uracil in DNA or thymine in RNA), include a feature-table entry using 'modified_base' with appropriate qualifiers (see modified nucleotide feature-table rules) to indicate this fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity symbols for nucleotides: use most restrictive symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an ambiguity symbol (representing two or more alternative nucleotides) is appropriate, the most restrictive symbol should be used (e.g., use 'r' for a or g rather than 'n'). The symbol 'n' is construed as any one of 'a', 'c', 'g', or 't/u' except where further described in a feature table; 'n' must not be used to represent anything other than a nucleotide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the narrowest ambiguity code possible to represent alternatives. A single modified or unknown nucleotide may be represented by 'n' together with a further description in a feature table. For sequence variants, use the ambiguity rules and refer to MPEP § 2412.05(c) for variant representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified nucleotide representation: prefer unmodified equivalent, otherwise 'n' with feature table
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified nucleotides should be represented in the sequence as the corresponding unmodified nucleotides ('a', 'c', 'g', or 't') whenever possible; any modified nucleotide that cannot be represented by a Table 1 symbol must be represented by 'n' and further described in the feature table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using 'n' to represent a modified nucleotide, include a feature-table INSDFeature with feature key 'modified_base' and mandatory qualifier 'mod_base' using a single abbreviation from Table 2 (or 'OTHER' plus a 'note' qualifier with the full chemical name). Do not use the abbreviation or full name of the modified nucleotide in the sequence field itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-table description of modified nucleotides (modified_base / mod_base)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each modified nucleotide must be further described in a feature table using the feature key 'modified_base' and the mandatory qualifier 'mod_base' with a single abbreviation from Table 2 (or 'OTHER' with a 'note' qualifier). If an abbreviation is used, the complete unabbreviated name must be provided in the 'note' qualifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For regions of consecutive modified nucleotides sharing the same backbone, jointly describe them in a single INSDFeature element; provide either the most restrictive chemical name covering the region or list the chemical names of all nucleotides in the range in the 'note' value. If an individual modified nucleotide has additional modifications, also describe it individually in the feature table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of regions of contiguous residues (joint description)
rubrics_metrics.description: A region containing a known number of contiguous 'a','c','g','t', or 'n' residues for which the same description applies may be jointly described using a single INSDFeature element with the INSDFeature_location syntax 'x..y'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use joint description to avoid redundant entries for long homogeneous regions. For variants, insertions, deletions, and substitutions, follow the variant representation rules in § 2412.05(c) and MPEP § 2413.01(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and inclusion of sequence variants
rubrics_metrics.description: A primary sequence and any variant (each disclosed by enumeration of residues and meeting the definition in § 1.831(a)/(b)) must each be included in the Sequence Listing XML and assigned its own sequence identifier. If a variant is disclosed as a single sequence with enumerated alternative residues, it should be represented by a single sequence using the most restrictive ambiguity symbol. Variants disclosed only by reference to deletions/insertions/substitutions should be included in the Sequence Listing XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correct feature keys and qualifiers for variant types (e.g., VAR_SEQ, VARIANT, misc_difference, replace/note qualifiers) as indicated by WIPO ST.26 paragraph 96 and MPEP cross-references. Ensure each variant that is enumerated has its own sequence identifier; do not rely on cross-reference descriptions alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino acid sequence representation: direction, numbering, and terminator handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Amino acid sequences must be represented in the amino-to-carboxy direction from left to right and the first amino acid is residue position number 1 (including pre-sequences, signal peptides, etc.). Disclosed amino acid sequences separated by internal terminator symbols (e.g., 'Ter', '*', '.') must be included as separate sequences when each contains at least four specifically defined amino acids, with each such sequence assigned its own sequence identifier. Terminator symbols and spaces must not be included in the Sequence Listing XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For circular amino-acid-only rings choose a residue 1 consistently. When encountering terminator-separated segments, split into separate enumerated sequences in the XML and assign identifiers rather than embedding terminator symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino acid symbol set and case
rubrics_metrics.description: All amino acids in a sequence must be represented using the symbols set forth in WIPO ST.26 Table 3 and only uppercase letters must be used. Any symbol used represents exactly one residue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use uppercase single-letter amino acid codes from the approved list. Do not introduce non-standard symbols into the sequence field; use the feature table to describe special or modified residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguity and unknown amino-acid handling ('X')
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an ambiguity symbol is appropriate, use the most restrictive symbol (e.g., 'B' for Asp/Asn rather than 'X'). The symbol 'X' is construed to be any one of the standard amino acids (list provided) unless further described in a feature table; a single modified or unknown amino acid may be represented by 'X' together with a further description in the feature table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'X' to represent non-amino-acid material. When 'X' is used, include a feature-table element with feature key 'UNSURE' and optional 'note' to describe the unknown or modified residue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of modified amino acids in feature table
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified amino acids (including D-amino acids) should be represented as the corresponding unmodified amino acids when possible; when not possible, represent them as 'X' and further describe them in a feature table. Use feature keys 'CARBOHYD' or 'LIPID' with 'note' for carbohydrate/lipid modifications, 'MOD_RES' with 'note' for other post-translational modifications, and 'SITE' with 'note' when the modified amino acid is not a post-translational modification. The 'note' must be an abbreviation from Table 4 or the complete unabbreviated name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the abbreviations or full names of modified amino acids in the sequence text. Put modifications into the feature table with the correct feature key and a 'note' giving either the approved abbreviation (from Table 4) or the full chemical name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint description of regions of amino acid 'X' residues
rubrics_metrics.description: A region containing a known number of contiguous 'X' residues for which the same description applies may be jointly described using a single INSDFeature element with INSDFeature_location syntax 'x..y'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use joint description to concisely represent repeated unknown/modified amino acids and to keep the feature table organized; follow MPEP subsections II–IV for proper feature-key usage and location syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations: non-contiguous segments assembled as single sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence constructed as a single continuous sequence derived from one or more non-contiguous segments of a larger sequence or from segments from different sequences must be listed in the Sequence Listing XML as described in WIPO ST.26 paragraph 35 and assigned its own sequence identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if constructed from disparate segments, present the resulting single continuous sequence in the XML with its own identifier and ensure the feature table documents the relationship to source segments per ST.26 guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations: contiguous 'n'/'X' regions with exact counts
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence that contains regions of specifically defined residues separated by one or more regions of contiguous 'n' or 'X' residues, where the exact number of 'n' or 'X' residues in each region is disclosed, must be listed in the Sequence Listing XML as one sequence and assigned its own sequence identifier (per ST.26 paragraph 36).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When exact counts of ambiguous residues are disclosed, keep them in the same sequence entry and document the counts; use feature-table entries where needed to describe the ambiguous regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special situations: gaps of unknown or undisclosed length
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence that contains regions of specifically defined residues separated by gaps of an unknown or undisclosed number of residues must not be represented as a single sequence in the Sequence Listing XML. Each region of specifically defined residues must be included as a separate sequence and assigned its own sequence identifier (per ST.26 paragraph 37).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot state the number of residues in an intervening gap, split the flanking defined regions into separate sequences in the XML with separate identifiers rather than attempt to represent an unknown-length gap within one sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive conformance to Sequence Listing XML and duplication in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequences disclosed by enumeration must conform exclusively to 37 CFR 1.832–1.834 (Sequence Listing XML) to avoid multiple formats in one application. Sequences included in the Sequence Listing XML should not be duplicated in drawings per 37 CFR 1.83(a), though drawings may be used when characteristics (e.g., sticky ends, double-stranded features, homology, protein structural features like epitopes) are best depicted graphically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include an enumerated sequence in a drawing for clarity, you must still include that sequence in the Sequence Listing XML and reference it in the drawing or Brief Description by sequence identifier (e.g., "SEQ ID NO:X"). Use drawings only where the Sequence Listing XML cannot effectively convey the desired structural/functional depiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML file format and encoding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing XML must be presented as a single file in XML 1.0 encoded using Unicode UTF-8, with character set restrictions per WIPO ST.26 paragraphs 40/41 and Annex IV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain elements (ApplicantName, InventorName, InventionTitle, NonEnglishQualifier_value) may use any valid XML Unicode characters except Unicode Control code points U+0000–U+001F and U+007F–U+009F. Reserved characters ' " & ' < > must be replaced as specified in ST.26. Ensure the .xml file conforms strictly to the technical form and format requirements of 37 CFR 1.834 and ST.26 to avoid non-conformance rejections.
